name: Email to Yan about leave of absence

content.text: need to email my advisor (dr. yan chen) to set up a meeting about taking a leave of absence to work on a startup full time. we have a 1:1 monday anyway (6/22). i want the email to give her a heads up so she isnt blindsided, not the full discussion. careful, respectful, not too long

Subject: Topic for Monday's 1:1

Hi Dr. Chen,

Before our meeting on Monday, I wanted to give you a heads-up about something I'd like to discuss. I've been thinking seriously about taking a leave of absence starting this fall to work full time on the research notebook project with Hudson, which has started to turn into a company.

I want to talk through what that would mean for my PhD, for the TutorTrace and IDETrace work we have in progress, and for the lab. I'm committed to finishing the UIST rebuttal and the NeurIPS submission process, and I'd like to hear your thoughts before I decide anything.

Thank you, and see you Monday.

Best,
David
she might worry about the camera ready and neurips rebuttal timeline too, those are aug. should i mention dates

Yes, one sentence with dates shows you've thought about it and lowers the stakes of the conversation:

> I'm committed to seeing through the UIST camera-ready (due August 14) and the NeurIPS rebuttal in late July, and I'd like to plan any leave around those.

Put it in place of the "I'm committed to finishing…" sentence. Keep the rest as is.
ok sending. what should i bring to the meeting

A short one-page plan helps:

- Proposed leave start date and length (e.g., Fall 2026, one year, revisit in spring).
- Status and owner of each active project: TutorTrace (camera-ready, talk in October), IDETrace (rebuttal, decision), anything with Minsun/Xiaohang/Rezky/Yue.
- What you can still do while on leave (e.g., the UIST talk) and what you can't.
- Funding: when your GRA ends and what needs to happen with Grace Kim / the graduate office.

And a question for her: what would make it easiest for the lab if you go? That shifts the meeting from asking permission to planning together.
